extra.message: Affected versions of cryptography are vulnerable to Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component / Out-of-bounds Read. The PyPI wheels for the cryptography package statically link a version of OpenSSL that contains security vulnerabilities (including a high-severity use-after-free in PKCS7_verify and several denial-of-service and forgery issues). Any application installed from an affected wheel ships the vulnerable OpenSSL binary, so an attacker may trigger out-of-bounds reads, crashes, or other memory-safety issues through cryptographic operations that reach the bundled OpenSSL code.

extra.message: Affected versions of PyJWT are vulnerable to Incorrect Authorization / Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity. PyJWT's JWS decoder does not enforce RFC 7515 `crit` (Critical) header handling: tokens that declare unknown critical header extensions in `crit` are accepted instead of being rejected. This can enable JWT policy/authorization bypass in deployments that rely on `crit`-signaled requirements (e.g., MFA/token binding/PoP such as `cnf`), and can cause "split-brain" verification where RFC-compliant components reject a token but PyJWT accepts it.

extra.message: Affected versions of pyjwt are vulnerable to Improper Authentication / Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature. PyJWT does not reject JSON Web Key (JWK) strings passed as raw HMAC secrets in `HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key`. When a verifier allows both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms and a raw JWK string is supplied as the verification key, an attacker can forge an HS256 token signed with the public JWK string used as the HMAC secret, enabling token forgery and authentication bypass.

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification). urllib3 fails to enforce its decompression-bomb safeguards in two streaming-API code paths: (1) the second and subsequent HTTPResponse.read(amt=N) or HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N) calls on a Brotli-encoded response, and (2) HTTPResponse.drain_conn() invoked after the body has been partially decompressed. A malicious server can return a highly compressed payload to force the client to fully decompress it in a single operation, consuming excessive CPU and memory.

extra.message: Affected versions of urllib3 are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. HTTP pools obtained from urllib3 ProxyManager via connection_from_url() or connection_from_host() do not strip sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, Proxy-Authorization) when following cross-origin redirects, leaking authentication credentials to the redirect target. Use ProxyManager.request() (the high-level API) instead, or upgrade to urllib3 >= 2.7.0.
